title: Transport of intrinsic Tor intervals
statement: For a finite commutative ring A, a scheme T, integers a ≤ b and any fixed-scalar pro-etale derived object K, the intrinsic realization D(F)(K) has HasProEtaleTorAmplitude [a,b] if and only if K has the standard fixed-scalar pro-etale derived Tor amplitude [a,b]. Both predicates test all module sheaves in their respective presentation. No comparison-origin or boundedness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YU, 08FZ; coefficient presentation via Modules on Sites, Tag 00YV

proof.text: Convert the standard Tor amplitude from lower and upper t-structure bounds into the separate homology-vanishing tests in degrees i<a or b<i. The characterization of the standard derived t-structure by homology gives both directions.

For the forward implication, choose a representative of D(F)(K′) and a K-flat resolution. For each fixed-scalar test sheaf N, test the intrinsic predicate at F(N). The single-test tensor-homology comparison identifies the zero object with F of the fixed-scalar tensor homology. Faithfulness and additivity of the equivalence reflect zero objects.

For the reverse implication and each intrinsic test sheaf M, essential surjectivity supplies N and F(N) ≅ M. For every representative and every K-flat resolution in the intrinsic predicate, apply the same single-test comparison. The fixed-scalar Tor bound and preservation of zero objects give vanishing. Adjoin the ordered interval hypothesis.

proof_origin.place: K-flat derived tensor and homology, applied to the canonical scalar-unit equivalence

theorem intrinsic_hasProEtaleTorAmplitude_iff_torAmplitudeIn
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (a b : ℤ) (hab : a ≤ b)
    (K : _root_.DerivedCategory
      (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)))) :
    Scheme.HasProEtaleTorAmplitude T A
        ((finiteCoefficientIntrinsicRealization T A).mapDerivedCategory.obj K) a b ↔
      ProEtale.DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn
        (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)) T a b K
